parsed.explanation: The combined operative regime imposes universal, traveller-facing federal exposure: every trans visitor crosses a border where sex markers are frozen at birth, X passports are no longer issued, officers must refuse or fraud-flag cases with document/appearance discrepancy, and foreign governments have documented detentions of trans citizens and issued travel advisories. Federal custody is documented as abusive (forced labour, beatings, sexual abuse, care denial). The state/province layer adds harsh document invalidation and a minor-care ban but no bathroom restriction, plus a hate-crimes law and local protections. Severe outcomes are mostly custody-bound rather than automatic, keeping this above the 0.25 band but solidly in Elevated Risk, especially for a travelling minor.

entry_documents.exposure: Documented: national policy forces birth-sex markers on passports/visas, X markers halted, case-note tag triggers refusal on discrepancy, and fraud findings carry lifetime ineligibility; trans travellers report confiscation and stranding; multiple allied governments issue advisories after detentions of foreign trans visitors.
entry_documents.protection: Not documented beyond pending litigation and an NGO legal-aid FAQ.
entry_documents.interaction: Entry screening is unavoidable for every traveller; a discrepancy can cascade into fraud investigation, detention, and removal under federal authority the state cannot displace.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Documented: national corrections policies impose care denial and 'conversion' regimens on trans inmates; immigration custody shows forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse of trans men; detention of foreign trans nationals over visa issues reported.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Any document dispute at entry can escalate into federal custody where the documented harms occur; state protections do not reach federal facilities.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal: executive order bars trans people from federally funded single-sex facilities congruent with identity. State: this state/province currently has no restroom restriction; local ordinances protect use; criminalisation proposals have died in committee.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Documented state/local non-restriction and protective ordinances, plus an injunction preserving school bathroom access.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Federal facilities remain closed; a pending state bill would impose birth-sex facilities and private suits if enacted.

care_services.exposure: Documented: gender-affirming care for under-18s banned statewide (surgery, blockers, hormones) after upheld 2023 law; federal rules threaten reimbursement bans and hospitals were subpoenaed for minors' records.
care_services.protection: Not documented for adult care availability.
care_services.interaction: A travelling minor cannot obtain care here; a parent travelling with a trans minor faces a legal care gap and records-exposure climate.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Documented: federal orders frame gender-affirming care as 'mutilation', target 'radically pro-transgender' groups in counterterrorism strategy, and delete transgender content from agencies; state marker ban described as forcing outing.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: State hate-crimes law includes gender identity as sentencing enhancement (operating force undocumented).
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Federal threat framing raises outing consequences and legitimises local hostility; state enforcement posture is mixed.

minors_guardians.exposure: Documented: minor's care banned; teachers face prosecution for facilitating social transition federally; state schools must notify parents of name/pronoun use; hospital records subpoenaed.
minors_guardians.interaction: An adult travelling with a trans minor faces care denial and school/notification exposure; minor alone cannot access care.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Documented arrest of a trans woman under a unit's bathroom law (elsewhere in country); 4 units criminalise facility use in circumstances; hate-crime coverage patchy.
street_violence_police_response.protection: State/province hate-crimes statute covers gender identity; no state bathroom criminalisation here; two cities protect restroom use.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: In this state/province street-level facility exposure is currently low; police response quality uncertain.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Open questions: which documents are believed at entry, adult care availability, hate-crime enhancement usage, fate of pending state facility bill and marker-ban litigation — all unresolved.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Active litigation and NGO documentation exist; several federal orders enjoined.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Litigation could ease or harden the regime; uncertainty cannot offset documented exposures.

anchor_checks.comparison: Weaker than 0.35-A: Vellandra's register can exclude visitors wholesale with no remedy. Here entry is possible but conditioned on birth-sex documents and fraud-scrutiny screening; consequences are refusal/detention risk rather than systematic denial, so this sits somewhat above 0.35-A but below 0.45-A's everyday checkpoint regime only marginally.

Similar to 0.45-C: pervasive identity-verification exposure woven into ordinary bureaucracy, with harm centring on investigation, fraud flags, document invalidation and care gaps rather than imprisonment. The federal custody abuses here exceed 0.45-C's severity, pulling slightly below it.

Below 0.55-B: Kestrel Isles' secondary screening ends in refusal or delay with functioning appeal desks. Here screening can escalate to fraud findings, lifetime ineligibility, and detention with documented custodial abuse, with remedies unresolved; the destination is a step materially harsher.

Well below 0.65-A: Vellmaris has national equality law that reliably orders release and produces compensation. Here the national framework itself is the exposure source, courts are only partly protective, and the state adds care and document restrictions.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller encounters a two-layer regime. The federal layer is the dominant exposure: universal, unavoidable document scrutiny enforcing birth-sex markers, an entry-fraud lever against discrepancy cases, foreign advisories corroborating real detentions of trans visitors, and documented custodial abuse — tier-1/tier-2 features under the precedence ladder. The state layer is mixed: among the harshest document-invalidation regimes and a minor-care ban, but no current bathroom restriction, protective city ordinances, and a gender-identity hate-crimes law. Protections do not reach federal facilities or custody, and pending litigation keeps outcomes volatile. Net: an Elevated Risk jurisdiction — clearly above the organised-targeting 0.25 band, but below any Reduced-Risk reading because every crossing and any custody episode carries the documented federal exposure, and a travelling minor faces a firm care ban.
